title: The MEV strategies always run the buy model: private sells get the buy fee ceiling (MEV_SELL_MAX_PRIORITY_FEE_GWEI is never applied), the documented "load-bearing" MEV_MAX_PRIORITY_FEE_GWEI cap is read nowhere, a sell reserves gas for a further sell, and the alerts tell the operator to change knobs that do nothing

evidence.note: buildReconcileConfig(env, sellGasLimit, maxRetries, leg = "buy"): the ceiling is MEV_BUY_MAX_PRIORITY_FEE_GWEI unless leg is "sell"
buildReconcileConfig(process.env, sellGasLimit, maxRetries): no leg, so "buy"
MevStrategy.sendTransaction has no buy/sell parameter, so a strategy cannot know it is selling
escalatePrivateSell calls sendTxWithRetry -> strategy.sendTransaction; the sell leg therefore runs with the buy ceiling
the only "sell" config is built for the no-double-sell guard, which uses only its confirm window and poll; its ceiling is never used
the public-fallback alert tells the operator to "raise MEV_SELL_MAX_PRIORITY_FEE_GWEI", which has no effect on any submit
no output: MEV_MAX_PRIORITY_FEE_GWEI, registered at config.ts:171 and .env.example:229 as the "load-bearing safety cap (default 5)", is read nowhere
the ceiling-hit alert tells the operator to "Increase MEV_MAX_PRIORITY_FEE_GWEI", which has no effect; the real ceiling is MEV_BUY_MAX_PRIORITY_FEE_GWEI (default 25)
on the sell leg (value 0, buyGasLimit = sell gas limit) the bound still subtracts a reserve for "the eventual sell", i.e. a second sell that does not exist
codex (22-27 independent second opinion, graded S1): Private sells use the buy priority-fee ceiling
codex (22-27 independent second opinion, graded S2): Selling requires funds for another future sell

sibling_sites_checked: All four buildReconcileConfig callers (flashbots.ts:182, passthrough.ts:83, bloxroute.ts:104 with no leg; bot.ts:577 "buy" and exitEngine.ts:940 "sell", both only for a guard reconcile window). All reads of the ceiling keys: MEV_BUY_MAX_PRIORITY_FEE_GWEI (reconciliation.ts:193), MEV_SELL_MAX_PRIORITY_FEE_GWEI (:192, reached only from exitEngine.ts:940), MEV_MAX_PRIORITY_FEE_GWEI (none). Operator texts naming the dead knobs: reconciliation.ts:607, exitEngine.ts:536. Cross-slice note for 22-28: TH-EXIT-23 records MEV_SELL_MAX_PRIORITY_FEE_GWEI as capping "the escalated priority fee of private sell attempts"; at the base SHA it does not (this entry); I did not edit the EXIT file.
severity_rationale: S2 OVERSPEND: the operator-facing cap is 5 gwei while the enforced ceiling is 25 gwei on both legs, so private priority fees can be 5 times what the documentation promises (300k gas x 25 gwei = 0.0075 ETH per attempt vs 0.0015); the affordability clamp still bounds total spend against the wallet, so the effect is bounded. The sell-side effects are indirect: an operator who lowers MEV_BUY_MAX_PRIORITY_FEE_GWEI to save on buys silently lowers the private sell ceiling too, raising the sell ceiling does nothing, and the phantom second-sell reserve refuses the private sell earlier on a thin wallet (public fallback instead, see AUD-TX-007).
recommendation: Phase 24 (card TX-02): pass the leg to the strategy (sendTransaction option) so sells use the sell ceiling and no second-sell reserve; decide what MEV_MAX_PRIORITY_FEE_GWEI means (remove it or make it the hard cap); correct the two operator messages. Behaviour-changing (fee ceilings), so it is a card decision.

sub_claims.claim: Private sells use the buy ceiling; MEV_SELL_MAX_PRIORITY_FEE_GWEI never reaches a submit
MEV_MAX_PRIORITY_FEE_GWEI is read nowhere although documented as the load-bearing cap
The sell leg reserves gas for a further sell
